styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small red barber chair with a white/grey chrome base. The upholstery has about 4 red steps (highlight, mid, dark, deep) and the base has 2-3 grey steps. The measured facts are in line with the simpler references: 12 colours per tile against 10 for the hedge, 0% flat-fill coverage, and 12 distinct colours against 11-14 for the bench, hedge and lamp. Dark edge pixels are 33% neutral, so the outline is mixed: some tinted dark red along the upholstery, some near-black/grey around the base. This is not a uniform black sticker line, and the 33% figure matches the well. Texture is limited to a few highlight and shadow dots on the cushions and no grain or speckle, which is less than the stall and well show. The chair is a small, compact object. Its ramps are a step or so shallower than the stall and well, but it sits comfortably next to the bench, hedge and lamp without looking flatter or more sticker-like. It is slightly below the richest references (stall 40 colours, well 38), but a careful artist would accept it as a simple furniture prop.
